note: The commonest word in Spanish. Also does possession: el carro de Ana, Ana's car. de + el contracts to del.
One word for all three. English fusses about the difference; Spanish does not.

sent.en: I will wait for you at the station.

note: a + el contracts to al. Also marks a person as the object: veo a Juan.

sent.en: We are going to the beach tomorrow.

note: Goes straight before the verb. Two negatives are correct: no hay nada.

sent.en: I do not want to go today.

note: One form for both singular and plural, and it never changes. Había is the past.
lo + adjective makes an abstract noun: lo bueno, the good thing about it.

sent.en: The best thing is to arrive early.

note: Also makes a verb impersonal: se habla español, Spanish is spoken.

sent.es: {Se} levanta a las seis todos los días.
sent.en: He gets up at six every day.

note: Before a noun: este carro. esta for feminine, estos and estas for plural.

sent.es: {Este} restaurante es el mejor de la zona.
sent.en: This restaurant is the best in the area.

note: For something near the listener. aquel is for something far from you both.
